Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
Ebony Kingdom preview is up
http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/index.php?line=Checklist_EbonyKingdom

Release Date: May 27, 2009

Blood of Africa!

Some stand outside the Thirteen, ancients who adhere to even older
traditions. They are the Laibon, the vampires born in the heart of
Africa, inheritors of secrets unknown to Camarilla or Sabbat. They too
have joined the Eternal Struggle &emdash; and they intend to thrive
there.

Ebony Kingdom

White Wolf's sixteenth expansion for Vampire: The Eternal Struggle is
a boosters-only set entitled Ebony Kingdom, and it revisits the
Legacies (clans) of the African continent.

Each booster pack contains 11 all-new cards randomly selected from a
set of 60 cards consisting of 20 rares, 20 vampires, and 20 commons.

Launch Event

White Wolf has scheduled the weekend of May 30th for the Ebony Kingdom
Launch Event.

Locate players in your area at www.white-wolf.com/vtes/member.

Order your Ebony Kingdom cards now at your local game and hobby store
or order directly from the online catalog.

http://store.white-wolf.com/Ebony-Kingdom-Booster-Display-P5617.aspx
http://store.white-wolf.com/Ebony-Kingdom-Booster-Pack-P5618.aspx

Guinea-Bissau Carnival

gains X+1 additional blood from the bank if succesful, where X is the
number of Aye he or she has. Burn this card during your next untap
phase. Only one Guinea-Bissau Carnival may be played in a game.

Messages.Author: jcrossn...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Rhavas wrote:
> This is a great point.  With the set not having any Aye or Orun in it,
> it means drafting with Legacies of Blood packs to make a lot of the
> cards useful.  Do many stores have a decent amount of LoB packs still
> around?

Drafting with LoB is not a viable option, even where packs are
available. The number of Aye and Orun one is likely to see from LoB
packs in a draft is far from sufficient to play the new cards in a
limited format. Note that the tournament organizer may give draft
attendees as many fixed additional cards as she likes, as long as
everyone gets the same cards. At a recent draft I ran involving
Twilight Rebellion, each player received 1 copy of Fee Stake: Baron,
which worked out really well. That said, if WW doesn't plan on
releasing Aye and Orun in plentiful quantities as promo cards, or via
some other method, some of the new cards look like they'll be fairly
hard to play.

Jesse

Messages.Author: D.J.
Messages.Body:


Which is absolutely irrelevant to draft, which is what Tony was
talking about.
And which is, definitely, a problem - Legacies of Blood is *already*
fair-to-mediocre for draft, and contains far too little Aye/Orun to be
worth mentioning, certainly not enough for cards or even draft effects
based on them to be useful in a draft setting.

Beyond that, too - really, there aren't "plenty" on the secondary
market. TheLasombra.com, for instance, has 5 Aye and 10 Orun
presently. There are currently 17 Aye available on Ebay, two for the
outrageous price of $1 each, and 23 Orun.

Assume a given average player bought a box of Legacies of Blood.
Heck, make it 2. They've got 4 and 4, currently, on average, if
memory serves about how distribution was in that set - it certainly
matches what I got. If you're really building to use them - say,
thinking you want to run Guinea-Bisseau as a bloat engine, and
assuming there's something comparable for Orun coming that's also
interesting - you're going to want at least 10 of them in the deck.
Probably more, but let's say 10. That means you need 6 more. So, you
and only THREE other players in the same situation will exhaust those
two sources on the secondary market at the moment.

That's not plenty. That's insufficient.

- D.J.

- D.J.

Messages.Author: henrik
Messages.Body:


I think you're underestimating recursion. And the discipline spread as
well.
Easy access to untap (Glutton, Freak Drive, Forced March) and stealth
(Forced March, Resist Earth's Grasp, random obf card) lowers the cost
of a successful action rather much.
The only thing I see Undele missing is superior Presence, and giving
him that would've made him really, really strong. That might be what
the Laibon clans need though, but I'd say the Ishtarri will do just
fine with this.
Ishtarri's clan disciplines is one of the strongest trio in the game,
and the fact that their vampires are limited (both in number and
through lack of superior clan disciplines) is what keeps them good
instead of broken.
